question: Who presides over the House in absence of the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker in the Indian political system?

options.text: Chief Justice of the Supreme Court

solution:
The correct answer is __**Chairperson so nominated**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In the Indian parliamentary system, when both the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha are absent, a **member appointed by the Speaker** presides over the proceedings.
 
• The Chairperson so nominated is selected from among the members of the Lok Sabha and performs the Speaker's duties temporarily.
 
• This arrangement ensures the smooth functioning of the House during unforeseen absences of the Speaker and Deputy Speaker.
 
• The role of the Chairperson so nominated is limited to presiding over sessions and does not extend to full powers of the Speaker.
 
• Such provisions are laid out in the **Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha** to maintain parliamentary decorum.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Speaker of the Lok Sabha:** The Speaker is the presiding officer of the Lok Sabha and is responsible for maintaining order and decorum in the House.
 
• **Deputy Speaker:** The Deputy Speaker is elected by the Lok Sabha members and acts as the presiding officer in the absence of the Speaker.
 
• **Rules of Procedure:** These rules govern the functioning of the Lok Sabha and include provisions for temporary presiding officers.
 
• **Parliamentary Decorum:** The presiding officer ensures adherence to parliamentary procedures and prevents disruptions during sessions.
 
• **Constitutional Provisions:** Articles 93 and 94 of the Indian Constitution pertain to the election and duties of the Speaker and Deputy Speaker.
